Alex / Tim — thanks for the context. I reviewed the attached redline quickly and sketched product impacts. My initial take:

Summary of what we can support with low engineering lift (<=2 sprints):
- Export of strictly defined telemetry fields at inference time: model_id (hashed), latency_ms, token_count, request_id (opaque), error_codes. Runtime flag to redact any additional fields.
- TTL enforcement: automatic deletion of these telemetry records after 30 days (configurable per-customer).
- Aggregation-only delivery to downstream vendors: we can support batch exports (1x hourly) with only aggregated metrics (no per-request PII or prompts).

Open product questions / blockers:
- If MedSys requires per-request IDs in the vendor feed (even if opaque), we need to understand use-case; per-request correlation increases risk and may require stricter encryption or enclave boundaries.
- Model-use clause: the customer asks that the data not be used to train models. We need contractual language and an enforceable technical control (e.g., deny-listing telemetry streams from any training pipelines).

Suggested mitigations (to propose to MedSys):
1) Contractually prohibit any use of telemetry for model training and require attestations from the analytics vendor.
2) Only allow aggregated exports by default; if per-request correlation is required, require encrypted envelopes with customer-managed keys and a documented justification.
3) TTL 30 days and soft-delete audit trail; retention above 30 days requires documented approval and product ticket.

Impact on roadmap: we have a telemetry export config story planned for Q4; the work to enforce TTL and aggregation export is alignable but will need a small scoped change to export pipelines. If MedSys needs per-request feeds or customer-managed keys, that will push to Q1 and require security signoff.

If Tim can answer whether the analytics vendor needs per-request IDs and confirm "no prompts/no outputs" are included, we'll draft a POA and a narrow acceptance criteria document for Legal/Security.

Thanks — Irene
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Team / Tim — security perspective and must-haves below. Overall stance: possible if strictly scoped and enforced. Proposed controls we need in contract + implementation before approving the carveout: 

Mandatory contract clauses (suggested language to Legal):
- "Telemetry Data" limited to anonymized inference metadata (latency, token counts, hashed model identifier, error codes). Telemetry shall not contain prompt text, outputs, or PHI/PII.
- Right to audit the analytics vendor once with 30 days' notice; vendor must provide SOC 2 Type II or equivalent evidence.
- Prohibition on using Telemetry Data for model training, fine-tuning, or improvement of the vendor's or customer's LLM models.
- Required use of encryption at-rest and in-transit; for per-request feeds require envelope encryption with customer KMS or proven vendor KMS with attestation.
- TTL enforcement clause: telemetry must be deleted within 30 days, with an auditable deletion log.

Engineering/security implementation controls: 
- Enforce allowlist of fields at the exporter (deny by default).
- Aggregation/export pipeline runs in a dedicated VPC/subnet with strict egress rules to only the vendor IP ranges.
- If per-request correlation is permitted, require a separate, approved cross-team design ticket and customer-managed keys; block for pilots unless explicitly approved by Security Director.

Evidence required before signoff:
1) Vendor SOC 2 Type II (or equivalent report).
2) Network egress plan (IP ranges / endpoints) and proof of enclave/VPC separation for exports.
3) A short security design doc describing TTL enforcement and deletion audit trail.

If MedSys agrees to aggregation-only exports and provides the SOC evidence, Security can sign off within 48 hours of receiving materials. If the customer requests per-request correlation or any prompt-level telemetry, that is a no-go for pilot without an elevated review and product changes.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Head of Security, Redwood Inference

All — taking the inputs from Product and Security, here is a concise path forward and proposed contract text (draft) we can offer to MedSys: 

Proposed short contract language (draft):
"Telemetry Data" means aggregated and anonymized inference performance metrics including latency_ms, token_count, model_hash, and error_code, and excludes any raw input prompts, model outputs, or any Directly Identifiable Health Information. Telemetry Data shall not be used to train, fine-tune, or improve any machine learning models. Telemetry Data will be retained for no longer than thirty (30) days, after which it will be programmatically deleted and logged. Subprocessors receiving Telemetry Data shall be subject to vendor security attestation (SOC 2 Type II or equivalent) and the Customer (Redwood or MedSys as applicable) shall have the right to audit once with thirty (30) days' prior notice.

Ask to MedSys: please confirm acceptance of aggregation-only export and the list of exporter fields (we need an explicit field inventory). If MedSys needs per-request correlation, confirm a business justification and accept that additional technical controls and time are required.

If MedSys confirms aggregation-only and provides SOC 2 evidence for the named analytics vendor, Legal can prepare an amendment to the DPA (1-2 business days). Security has agreed signoff conditions above. Product has a small scoped change planned that can be fast-tracked for this pilot.

Alex — can you ask Tim to send the vendor SOC 2 report and confirm the exact fields required (field inventory) by EOD Thursday 2026-10-06? If we have those, Legal + Security can sign off and we can return an edited DPA.

Ben Carter
